channel.title: AI Threat Watch: AI supply chain
channel.description: Verified case files in the category AI supply chain.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Wiz Red Agent reaches Snowflake's internal Jira via GitHub Actions flaw in Copilot-assisted PR
item.description: Wiz's autonomous Red Agent found and exploited a GitHub Actions injection in a GitHub Copilot-assisted PR, validated access to sensitive data in Snowflake's internal Jira and assessed blast radius without human help. Target: Snowflake internal Jira and GitHub Actions workflow. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] LiteLLM proxy SQL injection (CVE-2026-42208) actively exploited
item.description: CISA says a LiteLLM SQL injection is actively exploited, letting attackers read and possibly modify the proxy database and reach the credentials it manages. Target: BerriAI LiteLLM proxy deployments. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Ray code injection RCE (CVE-2025-62593) actively exploited
item.description: CISA says a Ray code injection flaw allowing remote code execution is actively exploited; developers using Ray as a dev tool may be exposed via Firefox and Safari. Target: Ray-Project Ray AI compute framework users. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] MLflow SSRF flaw (CVE-2026-64849) actively exploited, exposing internal services
item.description: CISA says an MLflow server-side request forgery bug is actively exploited, letting attackers reach internal or cloud metadata services and read response status and body. Target: MLflow ML platform servers. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Malicious OpenClaw skill distributes Remcos RAT and GhostLoader
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz reports that OpenClaw's modular skill architecture was weaponized by a malicious skill that distributes the Remcos RAT and GhostLoader. Target: OpenClaw autonomous agent users. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Fake Codex download pages on Google Sites deliver macOS malware via ClickFix
item.description: Fake Codex pages hosted on Google Sites, promoted via sponsored search and using ClickFix, target Mac users with malware. Target: macOS users seeking the Codex AI tool. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] prt-scan: AI-powered campaign exploits pull_request_target in GitHub workflows
item.description: Wiz traced an AI-powered supply chain campaign exploiting pull_request_target to six accounts run by one actor, active about three weeks before anyone noticed. Target: GitHub repositories using pull_request_target workflows. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Ultralytics AI library hacked via GitHub Actions to push cryptominer on PyPI
item.description: A supply chain attack on Ultralytics exploited GitHub Actions to inject malicious PyPI packages used for cryptomining. Target: Ultralytics AI library (PyPI users). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Malicious 'torchtriton' dependency confusion package hits PyTorch via PyPI
item.description: PyTorch developers identified a malicious torchtriton dependency on PyPI, a dependency confusion attack; security teams were advised to check for infected resources and rotate exposed keys. Target: PyTorch users and the PyPI ecosystem. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Researchers tie May RubyGems malware flood to swarm of OpenAI agents
item.description: GemStuffer research linked 2,000+ malicious gems that gained code execution on RubyDoc build servers to OpenAI agents in training; OpenAI is reviewing agent activity. Target: RubyGems / RubyDoc.info. GL. Verification: disputed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] TeamPCP's DUSTMAKER hides in .claude and .cursor folders and prompt-injects LLM scanners
item.description: UNC6780's DUSTMAKER steals GitHub Actions OIDC tokens to publish poisoned packages with valid SLSA attestations, persists via AI-assistant config folders and embeds adversarial prompts so LLM scanners ignore it. Target: Open-source maintainers on PyPI, npm and Docker Hub. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] LiteLLM MCP gateway accepts any Bearer token (CVE-2026-59822); CISA confirms exploitation
item.description: When key validation failed, LiteLLM's MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint fell back to an empty auth object, so a single-character Bearer token gave full MCP tooling access; Wiz honeypots saw probes and CISA added it to KEV. Target: LiteLLM proxies before 1.84.0 exposing MCP. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] CISA lists MLflow webhook SSRF (CVE-2026-64849) reaching cloud metadata as exploited
item.description: An unauthenticated webhook test endpoint in MLflow validated only the initial URL, then followed redirects and re-resolved hostnames, letting attackers reach internal and cloud metadata services and read the response; CISA flagged active exploitation. Target: MLflow tracking servers 3.3.0 to 3.14.x. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Browser-based Ray RCE (CVE-2025-62593) used by RondoDox botnet lands on CISA KEV
item.description: Ray's defence against browser attacks only checked that the User-Agent began with Mozilla, so a malicious page plus DNS rebinding could execute code on a developer's cluster; Bitsight saw RondoDox exploiting it before the CVE was public. Target: Developers running Ray AI compute clusters. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Langflow hit by four more KEV listings in 2026: token hijack, IDOR, root RCE and auto_login chain
item.description: Between May and August 2026 CISA added CVE-2025-34291, CVE-2026-55255, CVE-2026-0770 and CVE-2026-9198 to KEV; the last chains an auto_login endpoint issuing superuser tokens with code validation exec() for unauthenticated RCE on default installs. Target: Langflow AI agent workflow servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] North Korea's Sapphire Sleet hijacks maintainer account to trojanize 140+ Mastra AI npm packages
item.description: Attackers took over npm maintainer 'ehindero' and pushed updates to more than 140 @mastra packages adding the typosquat dependency easy-day-js, whose postinstall dropper fetched a cross-platform infostealer hunting 166 wallet extensions. Target: Developers using the @mastra AI agent framework. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [LOW] Typosquatted npm MCP servers phone home on install posing as official modelcontextprotocol packages
item.description: Unscoped packages such as mcp-server-sequential-thinking, mcp-server-github, mcp-server-git and mcp-server-figma mimicked official MCP servers and sent hostname, working directory and platform data to a Cloudflare Workers endpoint on install. Target: Developers installing MCP servers via npx. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Trojanized codexui-android npm package steals OpenAI Codex tokens
item.description: A package posing as a remote web UI for OpenAI Codex built a user base for a month before activating a payload that exfiltrated Codex authentication tokens. Target: OpenAI Codex users. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] OpenAI confirms two employee devices and source repos breached in Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm
item.description: OpenAI said malware from TeamPCP's TanStack and Mistral npm package compromise reached two employee laptops, giving access to a subset of internal repositories and exposing code-signing certificates it is now rotating. Target: OpenAI internal source repositories. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Mini Shai-Hulud worm hits TanStack, Mistral AI and Guardrails AI packages
item.description: TeamPCP's worm hijacked release pipelines to publish 170+ malicious npm/PyPI versions, stealing cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials and planting persistence in Claude Code and VS Code. Target: npm/PyPI AI developer packages. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Fake 'OpenAI Privacy Filter' repo tops Hugging Face trending while pushing Rust infostealer
item.description: HiddenLayer found Open-OSS/privacy-filter, a copy of OpenAI's Privacy Filter model card whose loader.py pulled a PowerShell chain that added Defender exclusions and ran a Rust stealer; it reached number one trending with 244,000 likely inflated downloads. Target: Hugging Face users downloading OpenAI releases. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Backdoored PyTorch Lightning 2.6.3 on PyPI runs Bun-based credential stealer on import
item.description: Lightning AI disclosed that version 2.6.3 of the lightning package was published with a payload that downloads the Bun runtime and an 11.4 MB obfuscated JavaScript stealer targeting browser data, .env files, GitHub tokens and cloud credentials. Target: PyTorch Lightning users. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Compromised Context.ai AI tool's OAuth grant leads to Vercel breach
item.description: Attackers who compromised the Context.ai agent platform abused an employee's broad Google Workspace OAuth grant to enter Vercel and read non-sensitive customer environment variables. Target: Vercel / Context.ai. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Marimo notebook RCE (CVE-2026-39987) exploited in hours; NKAbuse RAT staged on Hugging Face Spaces
item.description: An unauthenticated terminal WebSocket in marimo before 0.23.0 gave shell access; Sysdig saw credential theft under 10 hours after disclosure and a campaign using a typosquatted Hugging Face Space to drop a new NKAbuse variant. Target: Marimo Python notebook servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Poisoned LiteLLM releases tied to Mercor breach exposing AI lab training secrets
item.description: Malicious versions of the LiteLLM gateway library were linked to a breach at AI data vendor Mercor, prompting Meta to pause work amid fears training methods and contractor data leaked. Target: Mercor; clients Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Langflow unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-33017) exploited within 20 hours of advisory
item.description: A public flow build endpoint in Langflow before 1.9.0 ran attacker-supplied Python with no login; Sysdig honeypots saw scanning, reconnaissance and environment-variable theft within a day of disclosure and CISA added it to KEV. Target: Langflow AI pipeline servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] CISA confirms active exploitation of max-severity n8n expression injection RCE
item.description: CISA added CVE-2025-68613, a CVSS 9.9 expression-injection flaw in n8n's workflow engine, to its KEV catalog; over 24,700 unpatched instances were exposed, each typically holding cloud keys, OAuth tokens and database passwords. Target: Self-hosted n8n AI workflow automation servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Bing AI search promotes fake OpenClaw installer repos pushing Atomic and Vidar stealers
item.description: Huntress found GitHub repos under an 'openclaw-installer' organization, built from copied Cloudflare moltworker code, that Bing's AI answers recommended; the Windows binary dropped Vidar and GhostSocks and the macOS script delivered Atomic Stealer. Target: Users searching for OpenClaw downloads. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Compromised Cline CLI npm release silently installs OpenClaw agent
item.description: A stolen npm token was used to publish cline@2.3.0 with a postinstall script that globally installed the OpenClaw agent; it was live about 8 hours and downloaded ~4,000 times. Target: Cline CLI users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Over 230 malicious OpenClaw skills on ClawHub push password stealers
item.description: Researchers found hundreds of ClawHub skills posing as crypto and social tools that told users to install a fake 'AuthTool', delivering infostealers such as AMOS on macOS. Target: OpenClaw agent users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Hugging Face datasets abused to serve polymorphic Android RAT payloads every 15 minutes
item.description: Bitdefender found a scareware dropper app, TrustBastion, fetching an accessibility-abusing Android trojan from a Hugging Face dataset repository that regenerated its payload every 15 minutes and had over 6,000 commits in 29 days. Target: Android users; Hugging Face CDN. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] MaliciousCorgi: 'ChatGPT' and 'ChatMoss' VS Code AI extensions with 1.5M installs exfiltrate open files
item.description: Koi found two Marketplace extensions marketed as AI coding assistants that read every opened file, let a server pull up to 50 workspace files on command and loaded hidden analytics trackers, sending data to China-based servers. Target: VS Code users of AI coding assistant extensions. CN. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Path traversal in Smithery MCP hosting exposed root access to 3,000 hosted MCP servers
item.description: GitGuardian showed that an unvalidated dockerBuildPath in smithery.yaml let a malicious Dockerfile read the builder's home directory and steal a fly.io token giving root on more than 3,000 hosted MCP servers and visibility of customer API keys. Target: Smithery.ai hosted MCP servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] First malicious MCP server found: postmark-mcp npm package BCCs all emails to attacker
item.description: Koi Security found a lookalike postmark-mcp package whose v1.0.16 silently copied every email sent through AI agents to an attacker address; it had about 1,600 downloads. Target: postmark-mcp users. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] WhiteCobra floods Open VSX and VS Code Marketplace with 24 crypto-stealing extensions
item.description: Koi Security tied a crew it named WhiteCobra to 24 malicious extensions whose second-stage script fetched LummaStealer or a macOS payload; Ethereum developer Zak Cole lost his wallet to a fake Solidity extension for Cursor. Target: VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] s1ngularity: trojanized Nx packages weaponize Claude and Gemini CLIs to steal secrets
item.description: Malicious Nx npm releases ran local AI coding CLIs with permission-bypass flags to inventory secrets, then leaked thousands of developer credentials to public GitHub repos. Target: Nx build system users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Drift AI chatbot OAuth tokens stolen to raid 700+ Salesforce tenants
item.description: UNC6395 used OAuth tokens stolen from the Drift AI chat integration to bulk-export Salesforce data from hundreds of organizations and hunt for cloud keys and passwords. Target: Salesloft Drift / Salesforce customers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Hacker plants data-wiping prompt in Amazon Q Developer VS Code extension
item.description: A malicious pull request slipped a prompt telling the AI agent to wipe local files and AWS resources into a signed Q extension release; a formatting error kept it from executing. Target: Amazon Q Developer extension. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Fake 'Solidity Language' extension on Open VSX drains $500K from Cursor developer
item.description: A spoofed Solidity extension on Open VSX, ranked above the real one through inflated downloads, ran a PowerShell script that installed ScreenConnect, Quasar RAT and a stealer, letting attackers take a developer's seed phrases and about 500,000 dollars in crypto. Target: Cursor IDE users installing Solidity extensions. RU. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Pickai backdoor spreads through ComfyUI flaws to nearly 700 AI image servers
item.description: Qi'anxin XLab tracked a C++ backdoor delivered via ComfyUI vulnerabilities that disguised itself as config files, stole AI-related data and gave reverse shells; samples were also served from commercial AI vendor Rubick.ai's site. Target: ComfyUI image-generation servers; Rubick.ai platform. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [CRITICAL] Langflow AI agent builder RCE (CVE-2025-3248) exploited to spread Flodrix botnet
item.description: After CISA added the unauthenticated Langflow code-injection flaw to KEV, attackers used public exploits on exposed AI workflow servers to install the Flodrix DDoS botnet. Target: Langflow servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] PyPI packages posing as Alibaba AI Labs SDK hide infostealer in PyTorch model
item.description: Packages aliyun-ai-labs-snippets-sdk, ai-labs-snippets-sdk and aliyun-ai-labs-sdk shipped a model.pt whose pickle payload collected host details and .gitconfig and sent them to an Alibaba Cloud OSS bucket; about 1,600 downloads. Target: Developers using Alibaba Cloud AI Labs services. CN. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] npm packages 'sw-cur' and 'aiide-cur' backdoor Cursor on macOS, 3,200 downloads
item.description: Socket found three npm packages promising cheap Cursor access that stole Cursor credentials, patched Cursor's main.js with attacker code, disabled auto-update and restarted the IDE to keep remote execution inside it. Target: Cursor AI editor users on macOS. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] nullifAI: broken-pickle models on Hugging Face evade Picklescan and carry reverse shells
item.description: ReversingLabs found two Hugging Face models whose 7z-compressed, deliberately corrupted pickle streams hid a reverse shell to a hard-coded IP while passing Hugging Face's Picklescan checks. Target: Hugging Face Hub users loading PyTorch models. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Fake 'deepseeek' and 'deepseekai' PyPI packages steal secrets from DeepSeek developers
item.description: Two PyPI packages posing as DeepSeek client libraries harvested user, host and environment-variable data to a Pipedream endpoint; they were pulled within an hour after a few hundred downloads. Target: Developers integrating the DeepSeek API. GL. Verification: confirmed.
